task_instance: Gate a candidate agent change against a baseline: using the skill's bundled sample result sets (8 cases x 5 trials each, with a critical-case and dropped-case scenario) as the baseline and candidate inputs, run the skill's regression_gate.py (plus flake_detector.py and trajectory_checker.py) to produce the paired-statistics merge verdict (PASS/WARN/BLOCK) with its blocking exit code.
blocker_detail: The skill's core deliverable is a statistics-first eval gate that is produced by executing three bundled Python stdlib scripts (trajectory_checker.py, flake_detector.py, regression_gate.py); the verdict is defined entirely by their computed output and blocking exit codes (e.g. exit 4 = BLOCK). The office-assistant runtime can only read/write/edit text files and fetch the web; it cannot run code, scripts or shell commands of any kind, so the scripts cannot be executed and no gate verdict/exit code can be produced or verified. The scripts are present next to SKILL.md, so this is not a missing-skill-file problem, and the run rules forbid writing my own replacement/hand-computed stand-in for what the scripts would output.
evidence: Read SKILL.md: workflow is three python invocations (python scripts/trajectory_checker.py, scripts/flake_detector.py, scripts/regression_gate.py) whose purpose is 'blocking exit codes' gating a merge. Read sample_baseline.jsonl (40 JSONL trial rows across 8 cases, including critical cases and varying pass/fail trials) as the concrete baseline input a user would supply. Producing the deliverable requires executing these Python scripts; the runtime grants no code/shell execution, which is the blocker. No files besides result.json were produced in the work directory.
